subject.title: Feature: --agent flag for TUI to select which agent handles the session

question: Should `openclaw tui --agent <id>` become a public startup selector, and if so what precedence should it have relative to `--session agent:<id>:...`, cwd workspace inference, remembered sessions, and global session scope?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear from source, but adding a public TUI CLI flag affects startup session ownership, model/auth routing, and remembered-session semantics, which are product/API decisions rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add the startup selector
options.body: Define `--agent <id>` as an additive public flag with explicit precedence and focused upgrade-safe tests/docs.

options.title: Keep current workarounds only
options.body: Continue supporting canonical agent-scoped session keys, cwd workspace inference, and post-launch `/agent`, then close or defer this request by maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Add the startup selector
recommendation.body: Define `--agent <id>` as an additive public flag with explicit precedence and focused upgrade-safe tests/docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact product gap and current blame/history place him on the relevant TUI startup files.
